business_model.claim: The company reports five shipping divisions: Bocimar (dry bulk), Euronav (crude oil tankers and storage), Bochem (chemical tankers), Delphis (container ships), and Windcat (offshore crew transfer).

Delphis specialises in medium-sized container ships. Windcat is a leading provider of safe and efficient crew transfer services to the offshore energy industry.

business_model.basis: stated in P3 (20-F Item 5, Revenue recognition)
business_model.claim: Revenue from voyage charters is recognised ratably over each voyage on a load-to-discharge basis, while time charter revenue is recognised ratably over the charter period; pool revenues are allocated on a time-charter-equivalent basis per an agreed formula.
quotes: Under IFRS 15, revenue from contracts with customers, voyage revenue is recognized ratably over the estimated length of each voyage, calculated on a load-to-discharge basis.
Revenues from time charters are accounted for as operating leases and are thus recognized ratably over the rental periods of such charters, as service is performed.
Through pooling mechanisms, we receive a weighted, average allocation, based on the total spot results earned by the total of pooled vessels

quotes: 4 super-eco dual fuel ammonia-ready VLCCs are on order with deliveries in 2026/2027 (CSSC Qingdao Beihai Shipbuilding) as well as two super-eco Suezmax with deliveries in Q2 2026 (Daehan Shipbuilding).

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (tanker market commentary with specific rate levels, sanctions timing, and fleet-supply data).
growth_thesis.claim: 2025 VLCC and Suezmax spot freight rates surged to the highest levels in years, with average tanker earnings almost double the 10-year trend and VLCC spot rates up around 80% in December versus the start of the year, driven in part by US/UK sanctions on Russian crude exports imposed in Q4 2025.
quotes: Both 2025 VLCC and 2025 Suezmax spot freight rates have surged to the highest levels in years. These levels are well above long-term averages – for context, average tanker earnings over 2025 were almost double the 10-year trend.
The US and UK sanctions – imposed in Q4 2025 – on Russian crude oil exports have created a surge in VLCC spot rates, which were up around 80% in December versus the beginning of the year.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (dry bulk market commentary with specific rate, utilisation, loading and scrapping data).
growth_thesis.claim: Dry bulk market conditions strengthened markedly in 2025, with Capesize spot rates surpassing USD 40,000/day and overall utilisation rising from 90.0% to 91.3%, supported by growing iron ore and bauxite trade from Brazil and West Africa.
quotes: In direct contrast to last year, dry bulk finished the year of 2025 very strongly: Capesize spot rates surpassed the USD40,000/day mark, as part of a longer term momentum that began in July following a slow first half of 2025.
Overall utilisation increased from 90.0% in 2024 to 91.3% in 2025.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (market commentary) and P3 (detailed sanctions and trade-realignment discussion in Item 5).
growth_thesis.claim: Sanctions on Russia, Iran and Venezuela have structurally increased seaborne shipping inefficiency and ton-mile demand by redirecting flows to longer-haul buyers in India and China and creating storage needs, a dynamic that benefits the company's tanker and dry-bulk divisions.
quotes: Iran, Russia and Venezuela sanctions have increased seaborne shipping inefficiency and the need to store crude waiting to be exported from those regions as traditional buyers sought alternatives (mainly India and China).

Russian crude and petroleum products that were previously sold to geographically closer European customers have increasingly been redirected to buyers in Asia, including India and China, generally resulting in longer voyage distances and a reconfiguration of tanker trading patterns.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in P1 (strategy description, fleet sections noting ammonia-ready specifications, and fuel-development description).
growth_thesis.claim: The company's stated strategy centres on fleet decarbonisation, with ammonia-ready and dual-fuel newbuildings across tankers, dry bulk, chemical and container segments, plus development of hydrogen and ammonia fuel production and storage to complete the clean-fuel value chain.
quotes: The strategy is centered around diversification and decarbonisation of the fleet: "Decarbonise Today, Navigate Tomorrow."
The group develops low-carbon solutions across all our divisions and also offers hydrogen and ammonia fuel to customers, through its own production or third-party producers.
CMB.TECH also works on developing hydrogen-powered industrial applications like trucks, locomotives and straddle carriers.
